mainTopic: מחוסר זמן in מעשר, defining טינוף, buying an animal of unknown history from a Jew, and the lump of blood that must be buried.
overview: The amud opens with a ברייתא showing that רבי שמעון lets a מחוסר זמן, an animal too young to be offered, enter the pen for מעשר, just like a בכור, which is holy at birth but offered later. The גמרא asks why מעשר is compared to בכור and not to ordinary קדשים. Each side has four similarities, so the גמרא concludes that רבי שמעון learns it from the גזירה שוה of 'העברה'. Next, the גמרא defines the טינוף discharge from the משנה: רבא calls it a murky discharge and שמואל calls it bubbles of blood. The 'חכם' who must examine it turns out to be an expert shepherd. רב חסדא asks how long an animal fetus takes to form, and the attempted answer from זעירי is pushed aside. The גמרא then asks about buying an animal from a Jew whose history is unknown. רב says its next calf is a sure בכור, שמואל says it is a doubtful בכור, and רבי יוחנן says it is surely חולין. A ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן does not refute the others, because with a בכור it is the buyer's job to ask. Finally, a new משנה rules that a lump of blood from a large animal must be buried, and the גמרא asks why it must be buried if it gives off no טומאה.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון lets a too-young animal be tithed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון: a מחוסר זמן enters the pen for מעשר, just as a בכור is holy before its time and offered after its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: an animal whose time has not yet come enters the pen to be tithed. These animals are like a בכור. Just as a בכור becomes holy before its time and is offered after its time, so too an animal whose time has not yet come becomes holy before its time and is offered after its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as proof of רבי שמעון's view: a young animal not yet fit for the מזבח can still be counted for מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A newborn animal cannot be brought as a קרבן until it is eight days old. Still, a בכור becomes holy the moment it is born and is simply offered later. רבי שמעון says מעשר works the same way: the young animal becomes holy now and is brought when it is old enough.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that is still too young (under eight days) to be offered
Enters the pen to be counted for מעשר בהמה
A firstborn male animal, holy from birth
Becomes holy before it is old enough to be offered
Is offered once it reaches the proper age

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: And it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
An animal lacking time enters the pen to be tithed,
phrases.notes: 'Lacking time' means it is under eight days old, too young for the מזבח.

phrases.english: and they are like a firstborn:
just as a firstborn is holy before its time
and is offered after its time,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מְחוּסַּר זְמַן קָדוֹשׁ לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ
phrases.english: so too an animal lacking time is holy before its time
and is offered after its time.

steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds a מחוסר זמן is included in מעשר בהמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא from רבי שמעון בן יהודה quoting רבי שמעון, comparing it to בכור
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מחוסר זמן becomes holy as מעשר now and is offered when old enough, like a בכור.

steps.title: Why compare to בכור and not to ordinary sacrifices?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון learns מעשר from בכור instead of from regular קדשים, which cannot become holy while too young.
steps.simpleTranslation: But instead of learning from בכור, let him learn from קדשים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison in the ברייתא: maybe מעשר should be compared to regular sacrifices instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Regular קדשים cannot be consecrated as a קרבן while the animal is too young. If מעשר were compared to them, a מחוסר זמן would not be tithed. So the choice of comparison decides the law.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary sacrifices that a person consecrates

phrases.english: But instead of learning from a firstborn,
let him learn from consecrated animals!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the comparison used in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of מעשר to בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קדשים are an equally possible model, and they would give the opposite result.

steps.title: מעשר is more like בכור in four ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בכור is the better model because it shares four features with מעשר: no redemption, blemish, substitute, and eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that he should learn from בכור, since they share: redemption, blemish, substitute, eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the comparison to בכור by listing four ways בכור and מעשר are alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Neither בכור nor מעשר can be redeemed. Both become holy even when blemished. A substitute for either is not offered. Both are eaten without being redeemed. Regular קדשים differ on all four points.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical / it makes sense
An animal swapped in as a substitute for a holy one

phrases.english: It is logical that he should learn from a firstborn,
since they share: redeeming, blemish,
phrases.notes: These words are memory cues. Each one is a point where בכור and מעשר follow the same law.

phrases.english: substitute, eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing בכור is closer to מעשר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: קדשים could just as easily be the model
steps.terutzMaskana: בכור shares four features with מעשר, so it is the better model

steps.title: On the contrary, מעשר is more like ordinary sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: קדשים also share four features with מעשר: male and female, holiness through people, not priestly gifts, and an ordinary animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn from קדשים, since they share: male, holy, gifts, ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the last answer by listing four ways מעשר is like regular קדשים and unlike בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור must be male, is holy by itself from birth, is a gift to the כהן, and has the special status of a firstborn. מעשר and קדשים are the opposite on all four points. So the logic now gives a tie, four against four.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly gifts given to the כהן
An ordinary animal, not a firstborn

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should learn from consecrated animals,
since they share: male, holy,
phrases.notes: More memory cues. For example, 'male' means a בכור must be male, while מעשר and קדשים need not be.

phrases.english: gifts, ordinary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the previous answer with an equal list on the other side
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logical argument that בכור is the better model
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: קדשים share just as many features with מעשר, so logic cannot decide

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns it from the word 'pass'
steps.stepSummary: Since logic is a tie, the גמרא concludes that רבי שמעון learns from a גזירה שוה: 'העברה' is said about both בכור and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי שמעון learns it from 'passing' and 'passing'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the logical comparison and says רבי שמעון's source is a word link between the פסוקים of בכור and מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שוה is a tradition linking two topics through a shared word. It does not depend on which case seems more similar. Since the word 'pass' appears with both בכור and מעשר, מעשר follows בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Passing', a word used for both בכור and מעשר
Linking two laws through a shared word in the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: The logical comparison ended in a tie, four against four. רבי שמעון includes a מחוסר זמן in מעשר because of the גזירה שוה 'העברה' 'העברה', not because of logic.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Shimon learns 'passing' from 'passing'.
phrases.notes: שמות 13:12 ('you shall pass', about בכור) and ויקרא 27:32 ('passes under the rod', about מעשר).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הַעֲבָרָה הַעֲבָרָה גְּמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the tie by pointing to a word link in the פסוקים
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון's source is the גזירה שוה of 'העברה', which links מעשר to בכור.

steps.title: What is a טינוף discharge?
steps.stepSummary: Starting a new topic from the משנה, the גמרא asks what kind of discharge counts as טינוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of טינוף?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a word from the משנה and asks what a טינוף discharge looks like. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a טינוף shows that the animal already gave birth, so its later offspring is not a בכור. The גמרא needs a clear definition so people know when this exemption applies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?
A murky discharge from the womb

phrases.english: What is considered a murky discharge?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition of the טינוף mentioned in the משנה

steps.title: רבא: as shepherds say, a murky discharge
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes the shepherds' saying: a murky discharge means the animal held a fetus inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: As shepherds say, 'A murky discharge: the animal held something in.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers using a known saying of shepherds about murky discharges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shepherds know from experience that this kind of murky discharge means the animal carried a fetus that did not come out whole. That is why it counts as a birth for the laws of בכורה.

phrases.english: Rava said: As the shepherds say:
A murky discharge: the animal held something in.
phrases.notes: He means the discharge shows the animal carried a fetus inside it.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טינוף is the murky discharge shepherds recognize as a sign of a held-in fetus

steps.title: שמואל: bubbles of blood
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a different definition: טינוף is bubbles of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Bubbles of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives his own description of what a טינוף is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a murky discharge, שמואל describes טינוף as blood that comes out in bubbles. This is a second way of identifying the discharge that exempts later births.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: Bubbles of blood.

steps.title: The discharge must be shown to a חכם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that the discharge must be shown to a חכם to decide what it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one must show it to a חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a practical rule: someone qualified must examine the discharge. This sets up the next question about who that is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every discharge is a טינוף, and a mistake affects whether a later animal is a בכור. So an expert has to identify it.

phrases.english: And one must show it to a wise one.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טינוף discharge must be examined by an expert.

steps.title: How would a Torah scholar know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a חכם, a Torah scholar, would know how to judge an animal's discharge.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חכם, how would he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the last rule. Identifying animal discharges is practical knowledge, not something learned from Torah study.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'חכם' usually means a Torah scholar. But this question needs hands-on experience with animals, so the גמרא asks who is really meant.

phrases.english: A wise one, from where would he know?

steps.title: רב פפא: an experienced shepherd
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'חכם' here means a skilled shepherd.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: An expert shepherd.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the 'חכם' is an expert shepherd, not a Torah scholar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'חכם' means someone skilled in this specific area. A shepherd who has seen many births can tell a real טינוף from other discharges.
steps.whatToRemember: A טינוף is a murky discharge (רבא) or bubbles of blood (שמואל). It must be checked by an expert shepherd, the 'חכם' of this rule.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חכם' does not mean a Torah scholar. It means a shepherd skilled in this practical matter.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: An expert shepherd.

steps.title: A human fetus takes forty days to form
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes a known rule: a fetus in a woman takes forty days to form.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: חכמים already said that a baby in a woman takes forty days to form.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא states a known fact about people. He is setting up the question he is about to ask about animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is a starting point, not a ruling about animals. Because we know the number for a woman, רב חסדא can now ask what the number is for an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Behold, they (the Sages) said; quoting an accepted teaching

phrases.english: Rav Chisda says:
Behold, they said:
the formation of the fetus in a woman takes forty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of טינוף and fetus formation by bringing in a known human timeframe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A human fetus is considered formed after forty days.

steps.title: How long does it take in an animal?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks how many days it takes for a fetus to form in an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא asked: In an animal, how many days does it take?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks a real question: we know the number for a woman, but what is it for an animal?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number for people does not automatically apply to animals. So רב חסדא wants a separate number for animals, which matters for knowing when an animal's discharge could be a real fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked; introduces a real question

phrases.english: Rav Chisda asked:
In an animal, how many [days]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the human forty-day rule and asks for the animal version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The number of days needed for a fetus to form in an animal.

steps.title: Maybe זעירי already answered this
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests that זעירי's rule, that there is no טינוף before thirty days, answers רב חסדא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Isn't this just what זעירי taught? זעירי said: There is no murky discharge in less than thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא tries to answer רב חסדא's question with a teaching of זעירי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a real discharge (טינוף) cannot happen in less than thirty days, it seems that thirty days is how long an animal fetus takes to form. That would answer רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this the same as...? Suggests the answer already exists

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Isn't this [the same as the teaching] of Ze'eiri,
for Ze'eiri said:
There is no murky discharge in less than thirty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an existing teaching as the answer to רב חסדא's question.
steps.raayaObject: The animal fetus forms in thirty days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זעירי's rule that there is no טינוף in less than thirty days.

steps.title: זעירי was talking about something else
steps.stepSummary: The answer: זעירי's thirty days refers to the time after a discharge when the animal will not accept a male, not to fetus formation.
steps.simpleTranslation: That teaching was said about accepting a male.
steps.whatsHappening: The suggestion from זעירי is pushed away. His thirty days is about something different, so רב חסדא's question stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי was not counting how long a fetus takes to form. He meant that after a discharge, the animal will not accept a male for thirty days. So his rule says nothing about רב חסדא's question.

phrases.english: That was said regarding accepting [a male].
phrases.notes: He means: for thirty days after a discharge, the animal won't mate. It's not about how long a fetus takes to form.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from זעירי by reading his statement as being about a different subject.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: זעירי's thirty days is about when the animal will mate again, not about how long a fetus takes to form.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חסדא's question about animals is left without an answer.

steps.title: What if you buy the animal from a Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה dealt with buying from a גוי. The גמרא asks what the law is when you buy from a ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found the case of someone who buys from a non-Jew. What about someone who buys from a Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. The משנה covered buying an animal from a גוי, and now the גמרא asks about buying from a fellow Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גוי, we cannot expect the seller to tell us about the animal's history. A Jewish seller might speak up, so maybe his silence tells us something about whether the animal gave birth before.

phrases.english: We have found [the law of] one who buys from a non-Jew;
one who buys from a Jew, what [is the law]?
phrases.notes: The case: the seller said nothing about whether the animal gave birth before, so we don't know if its next calf is a בכור.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצִינוּ לוֹקֵחַ מִגּוֹי, לוֹקֵחַ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, moving from the משנה's case of a גוי seller to a Jewish seller.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The בכור status of the next calf when you buy an animal from a Jew and its history is unknown.

steps.title: רב: It is surely a בכור
steps.stepSummary: רב says the next calf is surely a בכור, because if the animal had already given birth, the seller would have bragged about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: It is surely a firstborn. If the animal had already given birth, the seller would have bragged about that to the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: since the seller said nothing, the animal never gave birth, so its next calf is a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that already gave birth is worth more to a buyer, because its next calf belongs to him and not to a כהן. A seller would surely mention that, so his silence shows it never gave birth.

keyTerms.meaning: it gave birth for the first time
to boast, to praise one's goods

phrases.english: Rav says: [It is] a definite firstborn,
for if it were so that it had [already] given birth,
he would surely have boasted about it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question about buying from a Jew.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The next calf is a definite בכור, because the seller's silence shows the animal never gave birth.

steps.title: שמואל: It is a doubtful בכור
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says it is only a doubtful בכור, because the seller assumes the buyer will slaughter the animal and does not bother to mention its history.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: It is a doubtful firstborn. The seller thinks the buyer wants the animal for slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב. He says the seller's silence proves nothing, so we are left in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller thinks the animal will be slaughtered, its future calves do not matter to him, so he would not mention them either way. His silence tells us nothing, and the calf is a ספק בכור.

phrases.english: And Shmuel says: [It is] a doubtful firstborn,
[since the seller] thinks: he wants it for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב by saying the seller's silence proves nothing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The next calf is a ספק בכור, because the seller had no reason to mention its history.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: It is surely חולין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the next calf is surely חולין, because if the animal had never given birth, the seller would have warned the buyer about the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: It is definitely non-sacred. Why? If the animal had never given birth, there would be a prohibition involved, so the seller would have told the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third answer, the opposite of רב: the seller's silence shows the animal already gave birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal had never given birth, its next calf would be holy as a בכור, and a Jewish seller would warn the buyer so he does not sin by treating it as ordinary. Since he said nothing, the animal must have given birth before, and its next calf is חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: to inform, to let someone know

steps.confusionAlert: רב and רבי יוחנן both learn from the same silence, but they reach opposite results. רב says the seller would have bragged if it gave birth, while רבי יוחנן says he would have warned if it did not.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says: [They are] definitely non-sacred.
What is the reason?
If it were so that it had not [yet] given birth,
since there is a prohibition involved,
he would surely have informed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view that reads the seller's silence the opposite way from רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The next calf is definitely חולין, because the seller would have warned the buyer if a prohibition were involved.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if the seller did not tell the buyer anything, the buyer may go ahead and slaughter. This fits רבי יוחנן's idea that a seller would speak up if there were a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבי יוחנן, who says the calf is non-sacred: If the seller did not tell the buyer, the buyer goes and slaughters and does not hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes a seller tells the buyer when there is a prohibition, so silence means there is none. That is the same reasoning רבי יוחנן used.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא was taught in agreement with him

phrases.english: It was taught [in a baraita] in agreement with Rabbi Yochanan,
who says [the calf is] non-sacred:
If he did not inform him,
phrases.notes: This ברייתא is about the rule against slaughtering a mother and its young on the same day. The seller didn't say he had sold the other one that day.

phrases.english: he goes and slaughters, and he does not hold back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from a ברייתא for רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's idea that a seller would speak up if there were a prohibition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lets the buyer slaughter when the seller said nothing.

steps.title: Does this disprove רב and שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether this ברייתא is a full refutation of רב and שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב and שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the ברייתא into a challenge against רב and שמואל. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a seller's silence means there is no prohibition, then רב and שמואל, who do not treat the silence that way, seem to be wrong.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav and Shmuel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא brought for רבי יוחנן as an attack on the other two views.
steps.kashyaTarget: The views of רב and שמואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the seller's silence as a sign that there is no prohibition, which goes against how רב and שמואל read the silence.

steps.title: Seller's job there, buyer's job here
steps.stepSummary: There is no refutation. In the ברייתא's case the seller is responsible to speak up, but in the בכור case the buyer is responsible to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the matter depends on the seller. Here, the matter depends on the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב and שמואל by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's case, it is the seller's duty to warn, so if he says nothing the buyer may rely on that. With a בכור, it is up to the buyer to ask about the prohibition. So the seller's silence does not prove there is no prohibition, and רבי יוחנן's reasoning does not bind רב and שמואל.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on buying an animal from a Jew: רב says the calf is a sure בכור, שמואל says a doubtful בכור, and רבי יוחנן says surely חולין. The ברייתא does not disprove רב and שמואל, because with a בכור it is the buyer's job to ask.

phrases.english: There, the matter depends on the seller;
here, the matter depends on the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם בְּמוֹכֵר תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא, הָכָא בְּלוֹקֵחַ תַּלְיָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing that the ברייתא's case and the בכור case are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (who is responsible to speak up)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A seller's silence always means there is no prohibition, so רב and שמואל are refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: A seller's silence shows there is no prohibition only when the seller is responsible to warn. With a בכור the buyer is responsible to ask, so the ברייתא does not refute רב and שמואל.

steps.title: A large animal that expels a mass of blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rules that a lump of blood expelled by a large animal must be buried, and the animal's next calf is not a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: if a large animal expelled a lump of congealed blood, the lump must be buried, and the animal is exempt from the law of בכור.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the ruling of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב about a large animal that expels a lump of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two rulings. First, the lump itself must be buried. Second, the mother is 'exempt from בכורה,' meaning a calf born to her later will not count as a בכור. This משנה is the base text that the גמרא will now discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: a large animal, such as a cow
a lump or mass of congealed blood
exempt from בכור status, so her next calf is not a בכור

steps.confusionAlert: Don't misread 'פטורה מן הבכורה' as saying the lump is not a בכור. It is the mother who is exempt: her next calf will not be a בכור.
steps.whyThisMatters: The burial rule is exactly what the גמרא is about to question.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
A large animal that expelled a mass of congealed blood,
that mass must be buried,
and the animal is exempt from the firstborn status.
phrases.notes: He means the mother. A calf she has later will not count as a בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It moves on from the discussion of a seller's and buyer's responsibility to speak up or to ask.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lump of blood expelled by a large animal must be buried, and the mother's next calf is not a בכור.

steps.title: The lump of blood does not give off טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that the lump of blood does not make anyone טמא, whether by touching it or by carrying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: it does not give off טומאה, not by touching it and not by carrying it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a ברייתא from רבי חייא about the lump of blood from the משנה. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching adds a fact the משנה did not mention: the lump gives off no טומאה at all, neither by touching (מגע) nor by carrying (משא). This seems to put the lump in a lower category than the משנה's burial rule suggests.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rabbi Ḥiyya teaches:
It does not impart ritual impurity,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the lump of blood from the משנה.

phrases.english: neither through contact nor through carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא about the טומאה status of the lump in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lump of blood does not give off טומאה by touching or by carrying.

steps.title: If it gives off no טומאה, why must it be buried?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since the lump is not treated as a source of טומאה, why does the משנה require burying it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it does not give off טומאה by touching or by carrying, why must it be buried?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts רבי חייא's teaching next to the משנה and finds a problem. If the lump gives off no טומאה, why bury it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that it gives off no טומאה suggests the lump is not treated as a real baby animal. But burial suggests it might be one, possibly a holy בכור. The גמרא wants to know what reason for burial is left. The answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: and since (introduces the reasoning of a challenge)

phrases.english: But since it does not impart impurity,
neither through contact nor through carrying,
why must it be buried?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר דְּאֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה לֹא בְּמַגָּע וְלֹא בְּמַשָּׂא, אַמַּאי תִּקָּבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי חייא's ruling on טומאה to challenge the משנה's burial requirement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the lump of blood must be buried.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the lump gives off no טומאה, it seems not to be treated as a baby animal. Then there seems to be no reason to require burial.
